questions.q:
(a) State the number of particles in one mole of a substance. [1]
(b) Calculate the relative formula mass, Mr, of aluminium sulfate, Al₂(SO₄)₃.
[Ar: O = 16, Al = 27, S = 32] [1]
questions.tip: The 3 outside the bracket multiplies everything inside: S AND all four O atoms.

questions.q:
When 12 g of magnesium burns completely in air, 20 g of magnesium oxide is formed.
(a) Calculate the mass of magnesium oxide formed when 3.0 g of magnesium burns completely. [1]
(b) Calculate the mass of oxygen that combines with 12 g of magnesium. [1]
questions.model:
(a) 3.0 g is 12 ÷ 4, so the mass of magnesium oxide is 20 ÷ 4 = 5.0 g.
(b) Mass of oxygen = 20 − 12 = 8 g (conservation of mass).
questions.tip: Simple proportion questions need no moles: find the scale factor and apply it.

questions.q:
2.92 g of hydrogen chloride, HCl, is dissolved in water and the solution is made up to 500 cm³.
[Ar: H = 1, Cl = 35.5; Avogadro constant = 6.02 × 10²³ /mol]
(a) Calculate the concentration of the solution in g/dm³. [2]
(b) Calculate the number of moles of hydrogen chloride dissolved. [1]
(c) Calculate the number of hydrogen chloride molecules dissolved. [1]
questions.tip: Convert cm³ to dm³ by dividing by 1000 before you divide the mass by the volume.

questions.q:
Calcium carbonate reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid.
CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂
[Ar: C = 12, O = 16, Ca = 40; molar gas volume = 24 dm³ at r.t.p.]
(a) Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide, in cm³ at r.t.p., formed from 1.50 g of calcium carbonate. [3]
(b) Calculate the mass of this carbon dioxide. [1]
ms: (a) M1: Mr CaCO₃ = 100 and moles = 1.50 ÷ 100 = 0.0150 mol
questions.model:
(a) Mr CaCO₃ = 40 + 12 + 48 = 100. Moles CaCO₃ = 1.50 ÷ 100 = 0.0150 mol. From the equation 1 mol CaCO₃ gives 1 mol CO₂, so moles CO₂ = 0.0150 mol. Volume = 0.0150 × 24 000 = 360 cm³.
(b) Mr CO₂ = 44. Mass = 0.0150 × 44 = 0.660 g.
questions.tip: Use 24 000 cm³ per mole when the answer is wanted in cm³.

questions.q:
0.270 g of a metal M reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. 360 cm³ of hydrogen is produced, measured at r.t.p.
2M + 6HCl → 2MCl₃ + 3H₂
[molar gas volume = 24 dm³ at r.t.p.; Ar: Cl = 35.5]
(a) Calculate the relative atomic mass of M and identify M using the Periodic Table. [4]
(b) Calculate the mass of MCl₃ formed. Give your answer to 3 significant figures. [2]
ms: (a) A1: M is aluminium (ecf from their Ar)
questions.model:
(a) Moles H₂ = 360 ÷ 24 000 = 0.0150 mol. From the equation, 2 mol M give 3 mol H₂, so moles M = 0.0150 × 2 ÷ 3 = 0.0100 mol. Ar = mass ÷ moles = 0.270 ÷ 0.0100 = 27. M is aluminium.
(b) Moles MCl₃ = moles M = 0.0100 mol. Mr AlCl₃ = 27 + 106.5 = 133.5. Mass = 0.0100 × 133.5 = 1.34 g (3 s.f.).
questions.tip: Use the mole ratio from the equation (2 : 3) — the most common error is to assume 1 : 1.

questions.q:
In the blast furnace, iron(III) oxide is reduced by carbon monoxide.
Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂
[Ar: C = 12, O = 16, Fe = 56; molar gas volume = 24 dm³ at r.t.p.]
(a) Calculate the mass of iron(III) oxide needed to produce 14.0 g of iron. [3]
(b) Calculate the volume of carbon monoxide, in dm³ at r.t.p., needed to react with this mass of iron(III) oxide. [2]
(c) State the volume of carbon dioxide formed, in cm³ at r.t.p. [1]
ms: (c) 9000 cm³ (ecf: same number of moles as CO)
questions.model:
(a) Moles Fe = 14.0 ÷ 56 = 0.250 mol. 1 mol Fe₂O₃ gives 2 mol Fe, so moles Fe₂O₃ = 0.125 mol. Mr Fe₂O₃ = 2 × 56 + 3 × 16 = 160. Mass = 0.125 × 160 = 20.0 g.
(b) Moles CO = 3 × 0.125 = 0.375 mol. Volume = 0.375 × 24 = 9.00 dm³.
(c) 3 mol CO give 3 mol CO₂, so 0.375 mol CO₂ = 0.375 × 24 000 = 9000 cm³.
questions.tip: Equal moles of gases occupy equal volumes at r.t.p., so CO and CO₂ have the same volume here.
